name: chem-r7
context:
Round 7. You APPROVED reaction scoring last round and named one remaining defect: that the design 'teaches that endothermic reactions are invalid or impossible moves rather than simply energy-requiring ones', citing the refusal of N2 + O2. That is now built and measured.

WHAT CHANGED. The sign of the energy is no longer a gate. A rearrangement is returned whatever its energy; a negative value is a COST, charged against the player's banked energy. Driving a reaction is what that means physically: photosynthesis runs on sunlight, the Haber process on heat and pressure, electrolysis on electricity. The only remaining refusal is affordability — you cannot drive a reaction you have not banked the energy for.

The engine now derives photosynthesis per carbon without being told about it: CO2 + H2O gives CH2O + O2 at 404 kJ/mol REQUIRED, against a real value of roughly 467 per carbon. An oracle asserts it comes out endothermic and within the right magnitude band, so a data change that makes plants work for free fails the test suite.

A CORRECTION TO YOUR EXAMPLE. N2 + O2 was never refused for being endothermic. There is no nitrogen-oxygen molecule in the library at all: NO and NO2 have odd electron counts and no closed-shell Lewis structure, so they are excluded for the same reason CO and ozone are. Your general finding was right and is fixed; the specific example did not demonstrate it, and it still returns nothing because no product exists rather than because the energy is wrong.

MEASURED BEFORE SHIPPING, because a mechanic nobody would use is not a fix. Per board there are 125.4 endothermic rearrangements available against 300.6 exothermic ones, so the option is common rather than a corner case. A player with one-ply lookahead who may spend banked energy beats one restricted to exothermic moves by +2.3% at t=3.91, winning 42 of 80 boards. That is statistically real and small, and it is documented as small. A deeper search might find more but has not been run.

FOR CONTEXT, the standing measurements this design rests on: correlation between selection size and score is 0.122 (assembly scoring was 0.843); a memorisation-free chemical concept beats the match-3 instinct by 35.5% at t=15.07; and the match-3 instinct itself now scores 21% WORSE than random.

questions.text: Is charging endothermic reactions against banked energy a faithful model of driving a reaction, or does it misrepresent where the energy actually comes from?
A +2.3% uplift at t=3.91 is significant but small. Is that enough to justify the added complexity of an energy bank and a spend decision, or should the mechanic be cut?
Do you accept the correction that N2 + O2 was refused for a missing product rather than for being endothermic?

Excluding NO, NO2, CO and ozone for having odd electron counts or resonance keeps the exact-valence rule honest but removes some of the most famous molecules in chemistry. Is that trade still right at this stage?
Name the most specific real chemistry this design still teaches wrongly.
